Each official translation is signed, dated and stamped by a professional, accredited translator, which is what Maltese institutions normally ask for. title: Cómo apostillar documentos de Colombia, México y España
heading: ¿Qué es la apostilla?
text: Guía ¿Qué es la apostilla? La apostilla es un certificado que se añade a un documento público, como una partida de nacimiento, un título o una sentencia, y que confirma que la firma y el sello son auténticos. La creó el Convenio de La Haya de 1961 y sustituye, entre países miembros, la cadena de legalizaciones en embajadas. Malta, España, México, Colombia y la mayoría de los países latinoamericanos son miembros. La apostilla siempre se emite en el país que expidió el documento. Una partida de nacimiento colombiana se apostilla en Colombia, no en Malta. Colombia La emite el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Cancillería) , en su mayoría en línea a través de su servicio de apostilla y legalización. La firma del funcionario que firmó tu documento debe estar registrada en la Cancillería; para algunos documentos, como los académicos o los firmados por entidades privadas, puede hacer falta un paso previo. La apostilla se emite en formato electrónico y se puede verificar en línea. México Quién apostilla depende de quién expidió el documento: Documentos federales (por ejemplo, de dependencias o tribunales federales): los apostilla la Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB) . Documentos estatales , incluidas las actas de nacimiento y matrimonio del Registro Civil y la mayoría de los documentos de universidades estatales: los apostilla el gobierno del estado que los expidió , normalmente en su oficina de legalizaciones y apostillas. Por eso, un acta de nacimiento de Jalisco se apostilla en Jalisco, aunque vivas en Ciudad de México. España Documentos del Registro Civil, judiciales y muchos administrativos : los apostilla el Ministerio de Justicia , que ofrece apostilla electrónica, o los Tribunales Superiores de Justicia de cada comunidad. Documentos notariales , como los poderes: los apostilla el Colegio Notarial correspondiente. Títulos universitarios : puede hacer falta un reconocimiento previo de la firma; consúltalo con tu universidad. Primero la apostilla, después la traducción En la mayoría de los casos, el orden ideal es: Consigue un original o una copia oficial reciente del documento. Apostíllalo en el país que lo expidió. Traduce el documento y la apostilla juntos, para que la autoridad pueda leer ambos. Algunos destinos piden además que la propia traducción esté apostillada o sea jurada. Depende del país donde la presentes, así que dinos el destino al pedir tu cotización y lo comprobamos antes de que pagues. Los requisitos cambian y varían según la autoridad. title: How to apostille documents from Colombia, Mexico and Spain
heading: What is an apostille?
text: Guide What is an apostille? An apostille is a certificate added to a public document, such as a birth certificate, diploma or court judgment, that confirms the signature and seal on it are genuine. It was created by the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention , and it replaces the longer chain of legalisation through embassies between member countries. Malta, Spain, Mexico, Colombia and most Latin American countries are members. The apostille is always issued in the country where the document was issued. A Colombian birth certificate is apostilled in Colombia, not in Malta. Colombia Apostilles are issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) , mostly online through its apostille and legalisation service. The signature of the official who signed your document must be registered with the Cancillería; for some documents, such as academic records or documents signed by private entities, an extra step may be needed first. The apostille is issued electronically and can be verified online. Mexico Who apostilles depends on who issued the document: Federal documents (for example, documents from federal agencies or federal courts) are apostilled by the Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB) . State documents , including birth and marriage certificates from the Civil Registry and most state university documents, are apostilled by the government of the state that issued them , usually through its legalisation and apostille office. A birth certificate from Jalisco is therefore apostilled in Jalisco, even if you live in Mexico City. Spain Civil registry, judicial and many administrative documents are apostilled by the Ministry of Justice , which offers an electronic apostille, or by the regional High Courts of Justice . Notarial documents , such as powers of attorney, are apostilled by the regional College of Notaries . University degrees may need prior recognition of the signature before the apostille; check with your university. Apostille first, then translate In most cases, the best order is: Get a recent original or official copy of the document. Apostille it in the issuing country. Have the document and the apostille translated together, so the receiving authority can read both. Some destinations also ask for the translation itself to be apostilled or sworn. This depends on the country where you will present it, so tell us the destination when you request a quote and we will check before you pay. Requirements change and differ between authorities. title: Sworn vs certified translation: which one do you need?
heading: Standard translation
text: Guide Standard translation An accurate translation with no signature or certificate. It is right for understanding a document, internal company use, or anything that is not being submitted to an authority. Certified translation An official translation issued, signed, dated and stamped by a professional, accredited translator , who takes responsibility for it being a complete and faithful translation of the original. This is what most institutions in Malta , the UK , Ireland and many other countries mean when they ask for an “official” translation. Sworn translation In some countries, only translators appointed by the state can produce translations with legal validity. In Spain , for example, a traducción jurada must be signed and stamped by a traductor-intérprete jurado appointed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Other countries, including Italy and parts of Latin America, have their own systems of sworn or public translators. If your document is going to Spain, tell us before you order. We will confirm whether the institution requires a sworn translation and how to obtain it. Apostilled translation An apostille confirms the authenticity of a public document for use in another country. It can be placed on the original document , and in some systems on the translation too. Whether the translation also needs an apostille depends on the destination country. See how to apostille documents from Colombia, Mexico and Spain . Quick guide For your own information: standard translation. For an authority, employer, bank or university in Malta: certified translation. For an authority in Spain: usually a sworn translation ( traducción jurada ). For an authority in another country: often a certified translation of an apostilled original, but always check the local rules. Requirements change and differ between authorities. Always check the current rules with the institution that will receive your documents, and ask us if anything is unclear before you order.
